title: Reasonability of independent multilinear evaluations
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $[n]$ that vanishes on every set of size greater than $k$. Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables on this space, each with finite fourth moment, mean zero, and third moment zero. Suppose $B\ge1$ and each $X_i$ is $B$-reasonable, meaning its fourth moment is at most $B$ times the square of its second moment. Then $F(X)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ has finite fourth moment and is $\max(B,9)^k$-reasonable.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of $[n]$
The random variables $X_i$ are mutually independent
Each $X_i$ is $B$-reasonable, including its fourth-moment bound
replaced: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n\in L^4$ be mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, with $\E X_i=\E X_i^3=0$ and $\E X_i^4\le B(\E X_i^2)^2$ for every $i$, where $B\ge1$. If $F(X)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ has coefficients zero whenever $|S|>k$, then $F(X)\in L^4$ and $\E F(X)^4\le\max(B,9)^k(\E F(X)^2)^2$.
